name: PermissionPrompt
summary: Pre-prompt that explains WHY the app needs a system permission BEFORE triggering the OS-native dialog. Renders a centered card with an icon, title (the consequence), description (the value), and two buttons — 'Not now' (secondary) + 'Continue' (primary, which then fires the native prompt). Reduces the deny-rate of platform permission requests by 2-3x. Covers camera, microphone, location, notifications, contacts, photos, motion, tracking transparency, biometric.

description.description: 1-2 lines explaining why the permission is needed and the user-side benefit.

keyboard: Tab - cycle between secondary and primary
wcag: 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (intentional, exit via secondary)
rules: Focus trap; initial focus on the primary button.
Escape activates the secondary, not just dismiss — 'Escape' MUST acknowledge the user's choice to deny.
The native OS prompt that follows the primary is the responsibility of the consumer.

do: Lead the title with the consequence: 'Enable notifications to track shipment delays'.
Pair every PermissionPrompt with explicit description text — the user must know exactly what they're trading.
Use the kind-paired icon (Bell for notifications, MapPin for location, Camera, Mic, etc.).
Use intent='primary' on Continue and intent='tertiary' on Not now.
Render PermissionPrompt AT THE MOMENT the user can clearly benefit — not on first launch.
dont: Don't trigger the system prompt without a pre-prompt — the deny-rate is 2-3x higher.
Don't paint the secondary button in danger red — denial is a normal user choice, not destructive.
Don't show the pre-prompt more than once per session for the same denied permission.
Don't mention 'allow' or 'deny' verbatim in the labels — those are OS terms. Use 'Continue' / 'Not now'.

changelog.note: Initial PermissionPrompt contract. Ten kinds. Pre-prompt pattern reducing system-prompt deny-rate.
